findings.text: Identifier FAULT_FLAG_WRITE corresponds to bit zero for write intent. Identifier FAULT_FLAG_MKWRITE corresponds to bit one for preparation to make writable. Identifier FAULT_FLAG_UNSHARE corresponds to bit ten for demand of exclusive copy. Identifier FAULT_FLAG_ORIG_PTE_VALID corresponds to bit eleven for trust in cached entry state.

Identifier FAULT_FLAG_ALLOW_RETRY corresponds to bit two for permission to release and reacquire locks. Identifier FAULT_FLAG_RETRY_NOWAIT corresponds to bit three for nonblocking retry behavior. Identifier FAULT_FLAG_KILLABLE corresponds to bit four for abort on fatal signal. Identifier FAULT_FLAG_TRIED corresponds to bit five as marker of prior attempt. Identifier FAULT_FLAG_INTERRUPTIBLE corresponds to bit nine for abort on generic signals.

Identifier FAULT_FLAG_USER corresponds to bit six for user origin. Identifier FAULT_FLAG_REMOTE corresponds to bit seven for operation on foreign context. Identifier FAULT_FLAG_INSTRUCTION corresponds to bit eight for fetch rather than data access. Identifier FAULT_FLAG_VMA_LOCK corresponds to bit twelve for range lock based fault path.

Teardown control uses a dedicated bitwise unsigned integer type. Clearing mode for youth and dirtiness uses a dedicated bitwise signed integer type. Identifier CYDP_CLEAR_YOUNG selects position zero for youth clearing. Identifier CYDP_CLEAR_DIRTY selects position one for dirtiness clearing.

Identifier FOLL_WRITE corresponds to bit zero for writability demand. Identifier FOLL_FORCE corresponds to bit three for bypass of access permission during privileged lookup. Identifier FOLL_ANON corresponds to bit seven for exclusion of file backed ranges. Identifier FOLL_HONOR_NUMA_FAULT corresponds to bit twelve for mandatory handling of NUMA hints.

Identifier FOLL_GET corresponds to bit one for acquisition of an extra reference. Identifier FOLL_DUMP corresponds to bit two for error on holes during capture. Identifier FOLL_HWPOISON corresponds to bit six for inspection of poisoned state. Identifier FOLL_LONGTERM corresponds to bit eight for indefinite holding under user influence. Identifier FOLL_PCI_P2PDMA corresponds to bit ten for acceptance of peer device pages.

Identifier FOLL_NOWAIT corresponds to bit four for starting needed transfer without waiting. Identifier FOLL_NOFAULT corresponds to bit five for forbidding population of missing pages. Identifier FOLL_SPLIT_PMD corresponds to bit nine for splitting huge middle entries before return. Identifier FOLL_INTERRUPTIBLE corresponds to bit eleven for allowance of signal interruption.

Dumpability width is two. Identifier MMF_DUMP_ANON_PRIVATE corresponds to position two. Identifier MMF_DUMP_ANON_SHARED corresponds to position three. Identifier MMF_DUMP_MAPPED_PRIVATE corresponds to position four. Identifier MMF_DUMP_MAPPED_SHARED corresponds to position five. Identifier MMF_DUMP_ELF_HEADERS corresponds to position six. Filter shift equals dumpability width. Filter width is nine. Filter mask covers that shifted window.

Identifier MMF_DUMP_HUGETLB_PRIVATE corresponds to position seven. Identifier MMF_DUMP_HUGETLB_SHARED corresponds to position eight. Identifier MMF_DUMP_DAX_PRIVATE corresponds to position nine. Identifier MMF_DUMP_DAX_SHARED corresponds to position ten. Default filter enables anonymous private and shared plus private huge pages plus ELF default. ELF default is either the ELF header bit or zero depending on build configuration.

Identifier MMF_VM_MERGEABLE corresponds to position sixteen for identical page merging eligibility. Identifier MMF_VM_HUGEPAGE corresponds to position seventeen for background huge page availability. Identifier MMF_HUGE_ZERO_FOLIO corresponds to position eighteen as history of zero huge use. Identifier MMF_HAS_UPROBES corresponds to position nineteen for probe presence. Identifier MMF_RECALC_UPROBES corresponds to position twenty for probe recheck need. Identifier MMF_OOM_SKIP corresponds to position twenty one for exclusion from out of memory selection. Identifier MMF_UNSTABLE corresponds to position twenty two for unsafe user copy.

Identifier MMF_DISABLE_THP_EXCEPT_ADVISED corresponds to position twenty three for denial of transparent huge pages unless advised. Identifier MMF_DISABLE_THP_COMPLETELY corresponds to position twenty four for total denial. Combined disable mask joins both positions. Identifier MMF_OOM_REAP_QUEUED corresponds to position twenty five for queued reaping. Identifier MMF_MULTIPROCESS corresponds to position twenty six for sharing across processes.

Identifier MMF_HAS_PINNED corresponds to position twenty seven as sticky marker of pinning history. Identifier MMF_HAS_MDWE corresponds to position twenty eight with a single bit mask. Identifier MMF_HAS_MDWE_NO_INHERIT corresponds to position twenty nine. Identifier MMF_VM_MERGE_ANY corresponds to position thirty with a single bit mask. Identifier MMF_TOPDOWN corresponds to position thirty one with a single bit mask for default search direction. Legacy inheritance mask joins dump filter with huge page disable plus MDWE plus merge any plus topdown.

Fallback values are zero when architecture provides no override. Identifier MAP_32BIT requests low address range. Identifier MAP_ABOVE4G requests address above four gigabytes. Identifier MAP_HUGE_2MB and identifier MAP_HUGE_1GB request huge page sizes. Identifier MAP_UNINITIALIZED requests uninitialized mapping. Identifier MAP_SYNC requests synchronous DAX semantics.

Legacy acceptance mask covers sharing mode and fixation and anonymity plus denial of writes and executability plus growth and locking plus reservation and population plus blocking behavior and stack use plus huge page support plus address size and huge size hints. Fragments show eighteen member options combined into one mask.

Identifier MM_FILEPAGES tracks resident file mappings. Identifier MM_ANONPAGES tracks resident anonymous pages. Identifier MM_SWAPENTS tracks anonymous swap entries. Identifier MM_SHMEMPAGES tracks resident shared memory. Identifier NR_MM_COUNTERS is the sentinel total following those four.

Struct page_frag holds a page pointer plus offset and length with width adapting to word size and page size. Struct page_frag_cache holds encoded page value plus offset and bias with width adapting similarly. Upper bound PAGE_FRAG_CACHE_MAX_SIZE derives from aligned thirty two kilobytes. Order PAGE_FRAG_CACHE_MAX_ORDER derives from that bound.

Struct tlbflush_unmap_batch carries architecture state plus required flush marker plus dirtiness marker when batched flushing is configured and is empty otherwise. Dirtiness demands flush before input output to avoid stale writable visibility. Struct lazy_mmu_state holds two byte sized counters for enable depth and pause depth.

Struct kmmio_probe links into a list and records start address plus length plus pre handler plus post handler plus private context. Type kmmio_pre_handler_t observes before execution. Type kmmio_post_handler_t observes after execution.
Each header defines a single inclusion guard macro that marks the header as seen. Guards prevent repeated inclusion and carry no behavioral semantics beyond idempotence.

Macro ALLOC_SPLIT_PTLOCKS reports true when spinlock storage exceeds word fraction. Bound PAGE_FRAG_CACHE_MAX_SIZE derives from aligned thirty two kilobytes masked against page size. Order PAGE_FRAG_CACHE_MAX_ORDER derives from that bound.
Helper mmf_init_legacy_flags restricts input to inheritable subset and suppresses deny write execute inheritance when no inherit is requested. Result never carries bits outside legacy mask.

Helper vm_acct_memory delegates page count to per cpu accounting with zero batching here. Helper vm_unacct_memory negates that adjustment. Helper mm_compute_batch has no effect here. Constant vm_committed_as_batch is zero.

Helper calc_vm_prot_bits maps read plus write plus execute to internal permissions plus architecture additions. Helper calc_vm_flag_bits maps growth plus locking plus synchronization to internal behavior plus architecture additions, with stack inhibiting huge pages when that feature is configured. Helper _calc_vm_trans scales a present source bit to target position and yields zero when either side is absent. Architecture additions are zero in this configuration.

Default protection validation accepts only read plus write plus execute plus semaphore and rejects any other bit. Default flag validation accepts all inputs. Default write execute denial support reports availability. Architecture specific alternates exist as separate variants.

Address space exclusion distinguishes shared hold from exclusive hold. Exclusive hold pairs with sequence protection and traced outcome. Shared hold is traced without sequence change. Release of exclusive hold pairs sequence closure with unlock. Downgrade preserves sequence closure while relaxing to shared hold. Killable and try forms report failure instead of blocking. Scoped guards bind acquisition to release. Contention query exposes semaphore pressure. Static initializer prepares the semaphore.

Sequence protection for address space uses initialization plus begin at exclusive acquisition plus end at release or downgrade. Speculative observation attempts a nonblocking sequence capture and later validates against concurrent exclusive activity, avoiding speculation when exclusive hold is already present. Disabled configuration provides no-op initialization and begin and end, with speculation always declining and validation always reporting conflict.

Range read participation requires address space lock held and live reference acquisition, with failure indicating reclamation race. Nested form accepts ordering subclass while simple form uses default. Exclusive range acquisition is a no-op when already held and otherwise killable, with disabled variant always reporting success. Attachment assertions are active in one configuration and empty in the other. Detachment requires exclusive hold on attached range and normally completes by reference drop with rare eviction of speculative observers, with disabled variant doing nothing. Modification of attached ranges requires exclusive hold. Lockdep markers track shared and exclusive participation. Lookup under read copy update returns null when disabled.
Lock tracing helpers emit start and completion events when tracing is enabled and do nothing otherwise. Two configurations exist, active and empty, selected by build.

Range lifecycle moves from attached to detached under exclusive hold, with reference count mediating visibility to speculative readers. Sequence moves from idle to exclusive between begin and end, with downgrade closing exclusive phase while retaining shared hold. Speculation moves from capture to validation, with retry indicating concurrent exclusive activity and requiring slow path.

Accounting helpers adjust committed totals by signed page counts. Protection and flag helpers translate user requests to internal bits. Batch helper accepts overcommit policy with no effect here. Legacy flag helper filters inheritance. Active probe query reports ongoing tracing. Range lookup under read copy update provides locked range or null.

Debug configuration treats virtual memory violations as fatal with contextual dumps for ranges and address spaces and pages and control blocks, with once variants limiting repetition and generic warning helpers forwarding messages. Release configuration reduces range and space checks to generic bug checks and page and control checks to compile time validation of conditions. Interrupt state check warns when interrupts are enabled in debug and does nothing otherwise. Virtual bug check traps in one configuration and does nothing in the other.

Killable acquisition can fail under fatal signals and callers must handle interruption. Try acquisition can fail under contention and callers must handle absence. Read participation can fail when reference acquisition races reclamation. Detachment normally observes zero references but narrow window can observe transient elevation requiring eviction. Longterm holding pins pages indefinitely under user influence and demands careful use.

Public helpers include committed memory accounting and unaccounting, protection and flag translation, shared and exclusive address space acquisition with unlock and downgrade, range read participation, and probe activity query. Each operates on address space or range descriptors without exposing internal semaphore or counter details.
